Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

least adverb and adjective

also the least, least of all, not in the least, smallest

classical

Ov. Ars 3.426: quō minimē crēdās gurgite, piscis erit
Ter. Ph. 1033: Minimē gentium

minimē

adverb, superlative of parum

least; not at all

As an answer, “not in the least”, “not at all”: Minimē; stronger, Minimē gentium, “not for the world” (Ter.).

Other words

  • minimus, minima, minimum — least, smallest; youngest

    adjective, superlative of parvus · also used · classical · Publil. Syr. N 32: necesse est maximōrum minima esse initia; Sen. Ep. 85.41: minimus Aethiops

  • minimum — the least; very little

    noun (neuter of minimus), with a genitive; also an adverb · also used · classical · Publil. Syr. I 57: quī minimum cupit; Hor. C. 1.11.8: quam minimum crēdula posterō

Examples

  • quō minimē crēdās gurgite, piscis erit

    in the pool where you least expect it, there will be a fishOv. Ars 3.426

  • is minimō eget mortālis quī minimum cupit

    the man who wants least needs leastPublil. Syr. I 57, quoted by Sen. Ep. 108.11

  • Ah, minimē gentium: nōn faciam.

    Oh no, not in the least: I won’t do it.Ter. Ad. 342

See also less, at least.

SourcesLewis & Short: parvus (minimus, minimē) · Lewis & Short: minime
